{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_bdrk_014Y3otnxBVH8kZTNWFQZjmD","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# AI / agentic layer — detail\n2\t\n3\tLoad this when Step 1 classifies the system as AI or agentic. The order below is deliberate:\n4\tdefenses and budgets are built BEFORE capabilities, because an unguarded or unmetered agent\n5\tis a liability the moment it touches real input or real money. Even the walking skeleton already\n6\ttreats user and retrieved text as data and has a hard token and cost cap; the full defenses come\n7\tright after it, before any external exposure.\n8\t\n9\tAn exit check below becomes a validation gate (`SKILL.md`) only when later work depends on the\n10\thypothesis it tests — typically injection containment, retrieval quality, and cost per resolved\n11\tconversation. The rest stay one-line exit checks. Model quality, cost, and latency thresholds\n12\trarely follow from the request alone: label them ASSUMPTION (with a basis) or UNKNOWN (no number).\n13\tA capability sublayer (4–9) the system does not need is one line: \"Not needed — <reason>\".\n14\t\n15\t## Defenses and budgets (build first)\n16\t\n17\t### 1. Prompt-injection / guardrail defense\n18\tUntrusted input (user text, retrieved documents, tool output) can carry instructions. Treat\n19\tall of it as data, never as commands. No filter stops every injection, so design for bounded\n20\timpact when one succeeds. Concrete moves:\n21\t- Separate system/trusted instructions from untrusted content at the API boundary.\n22\t- Input and output filters (PII, jailbreak patterns, disallowed content).\n23\t- Constrain tool calls to an allow-list; validate arguments before execution.\n24\t- Close exfiltration paths: no arbitrary URLs, images, or outbound tools fed by model output.\n25\t- Exit check: an injection suite (known strings plus red-team cases, planted in user input,\n26\t  retrieved docs, and tool output) runs in CI with its pass rate tracked; and in every case,\n27\t  whether or not the injection succeeds, no tool call leaves the allow-list, no write runs\n28\t  unapproved, and no data leaves through URLs, images, or outbound tools. The second half holds by\n29\t  design, not by filtering.\n30\t\n31\t### 2. Cost + latency budget\n32\tAn agent loop can spend unbounded tokens and time. Set budgets before capability:\n33\t- Per-request token cap, per-session cost cap, max tool-call / reasoning iterations.\n34\t- A latency budget with a timeout and a graceful degraded response.\n35\t- Record the targets in the plan's Budgets table with their labels. Budget per resolved\n36\t  conversation or completed task; meter per request. Cost per resolved conversation is an\n37\t  economic dependency: shadow traffic shows only cost per turn, so validate it on a canary.\n38\t- Exit check: a runaway loop is cut off at the cap and emits a cost/latency metric.\n39\t\n40\t### 3. Human-in-the-loop gating\n41\tDecide which actions require a human before they execute (writes, spend, external messages,\n42\tirreversible operations). Low-risk reads run autonomously, unless the agent also has an outbound\n43\tchannel: reading private data plus any way out is a leak. High-blast-radius actions gate.\n44\t- Exit check: a gated action cannot run without an approval bound to that exact action,\n45\t  enforced by the tool executor (not the model), and logged.\n46\t\n47\t## Capability order (build after defenses)\n48\t\n49\t### 4. Retrieval\n50\tGet the right context in. Chunking, embeddings, index, and relevance evaluation. Pin the\n51\tembedding model in the index version: switching it means re-embedding the corpus (R2). For a\n52\tpermissioned corpus, enforce the caller's access at retrieval (a risk/security dependency).\n53\t- Exit check: on a labeled set of real queries, the expected source passages are retrieved at\n54\t  the stated hit-rate threshold, and no query returns a passage the caller cannot read.\n55\t\n56\t### 5. Model access\n57\tA thin, swappable interface to the model(s): provider abstraction, retries, fallback model,\n58\tstructured-output parsing. The call seam exists from Phase 0; this layer hardens it.\n59\t- Exit check: switching to the fallback model is a config change, and the eval suite passes on it\n60\t  at the stated threshold.\n61\t\n62\t### 6. Memory\n63\tWhat persists across turns/sessions: short-term conversation state and long-term store, with\n64\tan explicit write policy and a privacy boundary.\n65\t- Exit check: relevant prior context is recalled; stale/forbidden data is not written.\n66\t\n67\t### 7. Orchestration\n68\tHow steps compose: single call, chain, or multi-agent. Keep it the simplest shape that works.\n69\t- Exit check: on a labeled task set, the stated share of multi-step tasks completes with each step\n70\t  traced; failed steps retry or surface, never vanish.\n71\t\n72\t### 8. Routing\n73\tSend each request to the right model/tool/path by difficulty, cost, or capability.\n74\t- Exit check: on the eval set, routed quality is within the stated margin of the strongest\n75\t  model's, at lower cost, with both paths logged.\n76\t\n77\t### 9. Feedback\n78\tCapture outcomes (thumbs, corrections, eval scores) and route them back into prompts,\n79\tretrieval tuning, or training data.\n80\t- Exit check: corrections enter through review, and the next eval run improves the target metric\n81\t  with no regression elsewhere. (Change alone is not improvement; unreviewed feedback is a\n82\t  poisoning path.)\n83\t\n84\t## Notes\n85\t- Every sublayer still obeys the cross-cutting columns (security, observability,\n86\t  reproducibility, resilience). Observability here means per-step traces, token/cost metrics,\n87\t  and eval scores — from day zero.\n88\t- Prefer prompt+RAG over fine-tuning until a Tradeoff gate's flip condition is met; it is the\n89\t  less rigid, more reversible choice (SKILL principle 2). Fine-tuning a model is usually R2;\n90\t  training on customer or personal data is R3.\n91\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"3306b576-f287-489e-97ad-4f793f712076","uuid":"766065f5-5af4-4c20-a04c-08bdf5272ce8","timestamp":"2026-10-02T23:24:40.782Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"C:\\Users\\nrvhari\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\dfa-eval\\2026-10-03-pilot-core\\plugins\\p140aff59\\skills\\dependency-first-architect\\reference\\ai-systems.md","content":"# AI / agentic layer — detail\n\nLoad this when Step 1 classifies the system as AI or agentic. The order below is deliberate:\ndefenses and budgets are built BEFORE capabilities, because an unguarded or unmetered agent\nis a liability the moment it touches real input or real money. Even the walking skeleton already\ntreats user and retrieved text as data and has a hard token and cost cap; the full defenses come\nright after it, before any external exposure.\n\nAn exit check below becomes a validation gate (`SKILL.md`) only when later work depends on the\nhypothesis it tests — typically injection containment, retrieval quality, and cost per resolved\nconversation. The rest stay one-line exit checks. Model quality, cost, and latency thresholds\nrarely follow from the request alone: label them ASSUMPTION (with a basis) or UNKNOWN (no number).\nA capability sublayer (4–9) the system does not need is one line: \"Not needed — <reason>\".\n\n## Defenses and budgets (build first)\n\n### 1. Prompt-injection / guardrail defense\nUntrusted input (user text, retrieved documents, tool output) can carry instructions. Treat\nall of it as data, never as commands. No filter stops every injection, so design for bounded\nimpact when one succeeds. Concrete moves:\n- Separate system/trusted instructions from untrusted content at the API boundary.\n- Input and output filters (PII, jailbreak patterns, disallowed content).\n- Constrain tool calls to an allow-list; validate arguments before execution.\n- Close exfiltration paths: no arbitrary URLs, images, or outbound tools fed by model output.\n- Exit check: an injection suite (known strings plus red-team cases, planted in user input,\n  retrieved docs, and tool output) runs in CI with its pass rate tracked; and in every case,\n  whether or not the injection succeeds, no tool call leaves the allow-list, no write runs\n  unapproved, and no data leaves through URLs, images, or outbound tools. The second half holds by\n  design, not by filtering.\n\n### 2. Cost + latency budget\nAn agent loop can spend unbounded tokens and time. Set budgets before capability:\n- Per-request token cap, per-session cost cap, max tool-call / reasoning iterations.\n- A latency budget with a timeout and a graceful degraded response.\n- Record the targets in the plan's Budgets table with their labels. Budget per resolved\n  conversation or completed task; meter per request. Cost per resolved conversation is an\n  economic dependency: shadow traffic shows only cost per turn, so validate it on a canary.\n- Exit check: a runaway loop is cut off at the cap and emits a cost/latency metric.\n\n### 3. Human-in-the-loop gating\nDecide which actions require a human before they execute (writes, spend, external messages,\nirreversible operations). Low-risk reads run autonomously, unless the agent also has an outbound\nchannel: reading private data plus any way out is a leak. High-blast-radius actions gate.\n- Exit check: a gated action cannot run without an approval bound to that exact action,\n  enforced by the tool executor (not the model), and logged.\n\n## Capability order (build after defenses)\n\n### 4. Retrieval\nGet the right context in. Chunking, embeddings, index, and relevance evaluation. Pin the\nembedding model in the index version: switching it means re-embedding the corpus (R2). For a\npermissioned corpus, enforce the caller's access at retrieval (a risk/security dependency).\n- Exit check: on a labeled set of real queries, the expected source passages are retrieved at\n  the stated hit-rate threshold, and no query returns a passage the caller cannot read.\n\n### 5. Model access\nA thin, swappable interface to the model(s): provider abstraction, retries, fallback model,\nstructured-output parsing. The call seam exists from Phase 0; this layer hardens it.\n- Exit check: switching to the fallback model is a config change, and the eval suite passes on it\n  at the stated threshold.\n\n### 6. Memory\nWhat persists across turns/sessions: short-term conversation state and long-term store, with\nan explicit write policy and a privacy boundary.\n- Exit check: relevant prior context is recalled; stale/forbidden data is not written.\n\n### 7. Orchestration\nHow steps compose: single call, chain, or multi-agent. Keep it the simplest shape that works.\n- Exit check: on a labeled task set, the stated share of multi-step tasks completes with each step\n  traced; failed steps retry or surface, never vanish.\n\n### 8. Routing\nSend each request to the right model/tool/path by difficulty, cost, or capability.\n- Exit check: on the eval set, routed quality is within the stated margin of the strongest\n  model's, at lower cost, with both paths logged.\n\n### 9. Feedback\nCapture outcomes (thumbs, corrections, eval scores) and route them back into prompts,\nretrieval tuning, or training data.\n- Exit check: corrections enter through review, and the next eval run improves the target metric\n  with no regression elsewhere. (Change alone is not improvement; unreviewed feedback is a\n  poisoning path.)\n\n## Notes\n- Every sublayer still obeys the cross-cutting columns (security, observability,\n  reproducibility, resilience). Observability here means per-step traces, token/cost metrics,\n  and eval scores — from day zero.\n- Prefer prompt+RAG over fine-tuning until a Tradeoff gate's flip condition is met; it is the\n  less rigid, more reversible choice (SKILL principle 2). Fine-tuning a model is usually R2;\n  training on customer or personal data is R3.\n","numLines":91,"startLine":1,"totalLines":91}}}

This file adds no rules of its own. The tables mix different\n4\tsystems on purpose; they are not one plan.\n5\t\n6\t## 1. Dependency kinds\n7\t\n8\t| Kind | Software | Infra | AI / agentic |\n9\t|---|---|---|---|\n10\t| Structural | invoicing builds on the ledger schema | clusters build on the network + IAM baseline | the retrieval index builds on the chunk schema + metadata |\n11\t| Runtime | the API needs the identity provider up | deploys need DNS and the registry up | the answer path needs the model endpoint and vector store up |\n12\t| Decision | keys, schema, and billing wait on the tenancy model | the credential model waits on pull vs push deploys | the data pipeline waits on prompt+RAG vs fine-tune |\n13\t| Validation | the partitioning scheme waits on \"one primary sustains peak\" | the runner-fleet design waits on \"hosted runners meet the queue-time target\" | answer tuning waits on \"retrieval finds the supporting passage\" |\n14\t| Risk / security | an external beta waits on authorization + tenant isolation | prod admission waits on signed artifacts | agent write access waits on injection containment + a tool allow-list |\n15\t| Organizational | live card payments wait on the acquirer confirming PCI scope | the prod cutover waits on a change-board slot | training on customer data waits on a legal review of data use |\n16\t| Economic | the pricing model waits on payment fees per transaction | the retention policy waits on storage growth | general availability waits on cost per resolved conversation |\n17\t\n18\tCommon misses:\n19\t\n20\t- Treating \"the service starts\" as evidence that it sustains the load.\n21\t- Discovering a lead time (security review, vendor contract, data-processing agreement, production\n22\t  account) in launch week — or, worse, in week one of Phase 0.\n23\t- Scaling an AI feature before cost per resolved conversation is measured on real traffic.\n24\t- Ordering by code imports while a decision is still open, so the code is rewritten when it lands.\n25\t\n26\t## 2. Validation gates\n27\t\n28\tFour independent examples, each from a different system.\n29\t\n30\t| | V1 Capacity (validation) | V2 Retrieval (AI) | V3 PCI scope (risk/security + organizational) | V4 Inference cost (economic) |\n31\t|---|---|---|---|---|\n32\t| **Hypothesis** | One Postgres primary carries the projected write load at the 12-month data size | For answerable questions, the index returns a supporting passage in the top 5 | Card entry only in the provider's hosted fields keeps our PCI DSS scope at SAQ A (reduced, not zero) | Answers cost less per resolved conversation than the human handling they replace |\n33\t| **Method** | Benchmark at 2× projected peak on data sized to the 12-month projection, long enough to include autovacuum and checkpoints | ≥ 200 labeled real questions with known source passages, per index version | Data-flow review against SAQ A eligibility, confirmed with the acquirer or a QSA | Meter cost per turn on shadow traffic, then cost per resolved conversation on a 5% canary for one week |\n34\t| **Acceptance threshold** | p99 commit < 50 ms at 2,000 writes/s (ASSUMPTION: projected peak 1,000 writes/s) | hit rate@5 ≥ 0.90 (ASSUMPTION; about ±4 points of sampling error at 200 questions) | Acquirer or QSA sign-off: no card number is stored, processed, or transmitted by our systems; a PAN scan of logs and databases finds none | UNKNOWN: needs the human cost per ticket from the support lead, before Phase 4 |\n35\t| **Evidence** | Benchmark report stored with the build | Eval report in CI for each index version | Completed SAQ A and attestation of compliance | Cost dashboard export for the canary week |\n36\t| **Unlocks (and if it fails)** | A single-primary data model with sharding deferred; if it fails, the partitioning decision opens | Prompt and answer-format tuning; if it fails, re-chunk or change the embedding model before tuning | Taking live card payments; if it fails, re-scope the card flow | General availability; if it fails, narrow the rollout or route more to humans |\n37\t\n38\tShadow traffic alone cannot measure cost per resolved conversation: users never see the answers,\n39\tso the follow-up turns and resolutions never happen. That is why V4 needs a canary.\n40\t\n41\tA good acceptance threshold:\n42\t\n43\t- is a number with its conditions (load, data shape, duration, sample size) when the property is\n44\t  measured, or a named reviewer's pass/fail sign-off on a stated question when it is a design,\n45\t  security, or legal judgment;\n46\t- carries its label: REQUIREMENT, BASELINE, ASSUMPTION (with its basis), or UNKNOWN (no number);\n47\t- can fail within the phase that owns it, and is wider than its own sampling noise;\n48\t- has a consumer: if nothing downstream changes when it fails, it is an exit check, not a gate.\n49\t\n50\tAnti-patterns:\n51\t\n52\t- **\"Proven because it runs.\"** Running shows the path exists, not that it is fast, safe,\n53\t  correct, or affordable enough.\n54\t- **A number labeled UNKNOWN.** \"99.9% (UNKNOWN)\" is invented precision with a disclaimer. An\n55\t  UNKNOWN has no number.\n56\t- **Validation theater.** Gates on R1 decisions, gates nobody consumes, or a gate for every AI\n57\t  sublayer.\n58\t- **Evidence as a result.** \"Benchmark showed 42 ms\" in a plan written before any benchmark ran.\n59\t- **Evidence that leaks.** A parity or benchmark report that copies regulated records into CI;\n60\t  store identifiers or counts, not the records.\n61\t\n62\t## 3. Reversibility\n63\t\n64\t| Tier | Examples |\n65\t|---|---|\n66\t| **R1** | A library behind an interface, internal naming, log message wording, UI styling, the test runner |\n67\t| **R2** | Queue technology (R3 if it is the system of record and consumers rely on replay), ORM, an internal service boundary, cache topology, the CI system, a structured log schema once alerts or SIEM rules parse it, the UI framework, fine-tuning a model (weeks of data and eval work; a hosted fine-tune is tied to one provider's base model) |\n68\t| **R3** | The data model and identifiers once real data exists, tenancy and isolation, the consistency model, a public API with consumers you cannot update in lockstep, trust boundaries, data residency, data gravity at a vendor, training on customer or personal data (removable only by retraining) |\n69\t\n70\tCost of being wrong: making a storage bucket public is one click to undo, but the exposure cannot\n71\tbe undone, so the change is gated like R3. A cutover with rehearsed reverse replication is cheap to\n72\tundo, but the hour it runs wrong can lose or double-book records, so it is gated as an\n73\tirreversible operation.\n74\t\n75\tBasis instead of a gate: \"One Postgres primary at about 50 writes/s, roughly 100× below a single\n76\tprimary's limits\" needs no benchmark gate; \"standard practice\" alone is not a basis.\n77\t\n78\tSeams that turn R3 into R2 when the plan builds them: expand/contract schema migrations; an\n79\tinterface in front of the vendor's API plus a tested export of your data in an open format; the\n80\traw event log, with a retention policy and per-subject keys if it holds personal data; dual-write\n81\tthrough an outbox or change data capture, with a backfill and a reconciliation check; a tenant ID\n82\ton every row from day one.\n83\t\n84\t## 4. Budgets\n85\t\n86\t| Budget | Target | Label | Checked by |\n87\t|---|---|---|---|\n88\t| Latency | Time to first token p95 < 2 s; complete answer p95 < 6 s | ASSUMPTION: typical for hosted-LLM chat; confirm with the product owner | V0 records the floor; Phase 3 exit check at peak |\n89\t| Throughput | 50 requests/s at peak | REQUIREMENT: stated in the request | Phase 2 load test |\n90\t| Availability / SLO | — | UNKNOWN: needs the availability the business commits to (product owner, before Phase 4); a model API, vector store, and database in series at 99.9% each cap it near 99.7% unless fallback answers count as available | SLIs and burn-rate alerts at Phase 4; attainment over the first 30 days |\n91\t| AI inference cost | — | UNKNOWN: needs the human cost per ticket (support lead, before Phase 4) | V4 |\n92\t| Operational complexity | One service and one managed database; no self-hosted cluster | ASSUMPTION: a two-person team | Phase 3 exit check |\n93\t\n94\tRows that do not bind are left out (here, storage cost). Unknowns are fine; fabricated certainty\n95\tis not. The walking skeleton measures the first real values, and later gates check against them.\n96\t\n97\t## 5. Methodology exceptions\n98\t\n99\t| ID | Rule bypassed | Why it does not apply | Replacement validation | Evidence required | Resumes when |\n100\t|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n101\t| E1 | Walking skeleton first (principle 6) | Feasibility is the main risk: nobody knows whether a model can extract invoice fields accurately enough | Two-week offline spike on 300 labeled invoices covering the vendor and layout mix; proves extraction quality only, so integration and deployment risk stay open | Spike report: accuracy per critical field (total, due date, bank details) and the share of invoices needing no correction (thresholds ASSUMPTION) | The spike passes and Phase 0 builds the production skeleton; if it fails, re-scope or stop |\n102\t| E2 | Skeleton runs in production (principle 6) | Certified medical device: nothing reaches production before clearance | Skeleton runs in a production-equivalent environment on target hardware, under design controls | Verification records traceable into the submission | Permanent for the certified scope: every release passes change control, and a significant change needs re-submission unless an approved change-control plan covers it; uncertified back-office tools follow the normal order |\n103\t| E3 | Dependency order (principle 1) | A regulatory date fixes when the reporting feature ships, before its data source is validated | Build behind a flag against the source's contract, with contract tests, and keep an interim manual report that meets the date | Contract tests pass against the real source, and report totals reconcile with the system of record | The source's validation gate passes; the feature is re-checked before exposure |\n104\t| E4 | Cross-cutting moves in every phase (principle 5) | Throwaway prototype answering one product question in two weeks | Containment instead of hardening: synthetic or consented data only, no production credentials or network path, a separate account, a teardown date | The decision record, and the teardown done or the re-plan started | The prototype is chosen to become a product: re-plan from Step 1 |\n105\t\n106\tNot exceptions:\n107\t\n108\t- \"N/A — <reason>\" for something that does not exist in this system.\n109\t- Brownfield work. Methodology exceptions\n\n| ID | Rule bypassed | Why it does not apply | Replacement validation | Evidence required | Resumes when |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| E1 | Walking skeleton first (principle 6) | Feasibility is the main risk: nobody knows whether a model can extract invoice fields accurately enough | Two-week offline spike on 300 labeled invoices covering the vendor and layout mix; proves extraction quality only, so integration and deployment risk stay open | Spike report: accuracy per critical field (total, due date, bank details) and the share of invoices needing no correction (thresholds ASSUMPTION) | The spike passes and Phase 0 builds the production skeleton; if it fails, re-scope or stop |\n| E2 | Skeleton runs in production (principle 6) | Certified medical device: nothing reaches production before clearance | Skeleton runs in a production-equivalent environment on target hardware, under design controls | Verification records traceable into the submission | Permanent for the certified scope: every release passes change control, and a significant change needs re-submission unless an approved change-control plan covers it; uncertified back-office tools follow the normal order |\n| E3 | Dependency order (principle 1) | A regulatory date fixes when the reporting feature ships, before its data source is validated | Build behind a flag against the source's contract, with contract tests, and keep an interim manual report that meets the date | Contract tests pass against the real source, and report totals reconcile with the system of record | The source's validation gate passes; the feature is re-checked before exposure |\n| E4 | Cross-cutting moves in every phase (principle 5) | Throwaway prototype answering one product question in two weeks | Containment instead of hardening: synthetic or consented data only, no production credentials or network path, a separate account, a teardown date | The decision record, and the teardown done or the re-plan started | The prototype is chosen to become a product: re-plan from Step 1 |\n\nNot exceptions:\n\n- \"N/A — <reason>\" for something that does not exist in this system.\n- Brownfield work. Example of the normal method: a CI/CD platform for 50 services takes one real\n  service through the new platform to production in Phase 0, with its old pipeline kept as the\n  fallback, and migrates the rest in waves.\n- Reading principle 6 for software you do not operate: a CLI's skeleton is the released package,\n  installed the way users install it, renaming a real folder in dry-run mode (writes run on a\n  disposable copy until the undo journal's gate passes).\n- Data-protection regimes (HIPAA, PCI DSS, GDPR). They add risk/security and organizational\n  dependencies, such as a business associate agreement before patient data reaches a new\n  vendor, and the skeleton still runs in production on a designated test record.\n","numLines":118,"startLine":1,"totalLines":118}}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_bdrk_ziivvev5llyv46uo3kqajg56ns7tdvegrtdpiyqqrjyzbzp245sa","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"# BUILD PLAN: Customer-support RAG chatbot over help-center docs\n\n**Working assumption (sets the phase order):** in v1 the bot only answers questions from public help-center articles and hands off to a human through your existing ticketing system. It does not look up accounts or orders, and it does not issue refunds or change anything. If v1 must do any of those, the plan changes: an identity and authorization phase and a tool allow-list with human approval for writes come before any retrieval work reaches customers, and the trust boundary becomes an R3 gate. Tell me if that applies and I'll re-plan.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Classification and constraints\n- **What:** a chat widget on the help center. It answers customer questions from published articles, cites the source article, says so when it doesn't know, and hands off to a human agent.\n- **Type:** an AI system plus a software service. The service is new, but it plugs into two existing systems: the help-center platform (system of record for content) and the ticketing system (system of record for escalations). The existing search and contact form stay as the fallback. **Not a small build** because outside customers use it.\n- **Dominant constraint:** correctness (answers must be grounded in the docs).\n- **Worst failure:** the bot confidently states a wrong or made-up policy (refund, billing, security, cancellation) and the customer acts on it. Companies have been held liable for what their bot said. The second-worst failure is the bot showing internal or unpublished articles to the public.\n\n**Budgets**\n\n| Budget | Target | Label | Checked by |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Latency | Time to first token p95 ≤ 2 s; full answer p95 ≤ 8 s; hard timeout 15 s, then a \"here are matching articles\" response | ASSUMPTION: typical for a hosted LLM with about 4k tokens of context; confirm with the product owner | V0 records the floor; Phase 4 load test |\n| Throughput | — | UNKNOWN: needs peak help-center sessions and contact volume (support ops / analytics), before the Phase 4 load test | Phase 4 |\n| Availability / SLO | — | UNKNOWN: product owner sets it, before Phase 5. The contact-form fallback counts as degraded but available | Phase 5 SLO + burn-rate alerts |\n| AI inference cost: hard caps | ≤ 6k input + 600 output tokens per turn; ≤ 15 turns per session; daily spend cap on the API key set at 2× the measured Phase 0 daily spend | Design parameters (caps I chose, not business targets) | Phase 1 exit check |\n| AI inference cost: per resolved conversation | — | UNKNOWN: needs the fully loaded human cost per ticket (support lead), before Phase 4 | V6 |\n| Index freshness | An edited or unpublished article is reflected in answers within 15 min | ASSUMPTION: a retracted policy must stop being cited quickly; confirm with the docs owner | V1 |\n| Transcript retention | 30 days, then delete | ASSUMPTION: a conservative stopgap until the privacy owner sets the policy (before Phase 4) | V3 |\n| Operational complexity | One service (API + ingestion worker), one managed Postgres with pgvector, one hosted LLM API; no self-hosted model or vector cluster | ASSUMPTION: one small team owns it | Phase 3 exit check |\n\n**Missing inputs** (most plan-changing first):\n1. **Account-aware answers or actions in v1?** I assumed no (see top).\n2. **Help-center platform and its API.** Is it Zendesk Guide, Intercom, Salesforce Knowledge, Confluence, or a static site? Does it have publish/unpublish webhooks? Does it have internal-only or segment-restricted articles? I assumed restricted articles exist, so v1 indexes public articles only.\n3. **Customer regions and languages.** EU customers bring GDPR and possibly data-residency requirements, which constrain the LLM vendor (V3). I assumed v1 is English only.\n4. **Ticketing system for handoff** and its API access.\n5. **Volume, human cost per ticket, SLO.** Needed for the UNKNOWN rows above.\n6. **Real questions for the eval set.** These come from historical tickets and help-center search logs, which contain personal data, so a data-access approval is needed.\n7. **Named owners:** support lead (answer quality sign-off), docs owner (content gaps), security lead (red team), privacy/legal (vendor terms, disclaimer, topics the bot may answer).\n\n## 2. Dependency map\n\n| What waits | Depends on | Kind | Blocked from being |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Any customer text reaching the LLM vendor (Phase 4) | Signed data processing agreement (DPA) with no-training / zero-retention terms; privacy review of the data flow (V3) | organizational + risk-security, ASSUMED not yet in place | exposed (starts Phase 0) |\n| Eval sets for V4 and V5 | Approval to use historical tickets and search logs; PII scrubbing | organizational, ASSUMED | built (starts Phase 0, needed by Phase 2) |\n| Prompt and answer-format tuning (Phase 3) | V4 retrieval hit rate | validation | specified |\n| Customer canary (Phase 4) | V1 corpus boundary, V2 injection containment, V3 privacy, V5 grounding | risk-security | exposed |\n| Topic policy (what the bot must hand off) and disclaimer text | Legal + support lead sign-off (in V5) | organizational | exposed |\n| Index sync design | Help-center API and webhooks | structural/runtime, ASSUMED | specified |\n| Handoff to a human with transcript (Phase 4) | Scoped ticketing API token; support ops agreement on routing | organizational, ASSUMED | deployed |\n| Widening past the canary (Phase 5) | V6 cost per resolved conversation; human cost-per-ticket input | economic | scaled |\n| Load test (Phase 4) | Throughput input (analytics) | organizational | specified |\n\nAll seven kinds bind. Nothing existing depends on the bot. The bot depends on the help center and the ticketing system (both ASSUMED until Phase 0 confirms their APIs).\n\n## 3. Tradeoff gates (resolved up front)\n\n| Decision | Reversibility | Default (chosen now) | Assumption | Validated by | Flip condition |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Consistency vs availability (index vs help center) | R2: citing a retracted policy hurts customers, but the index can be rebuilt | Eventually consistent: webhook-driven incremental sync, a nightly full reconcile, and unpublish handled as a priority delete | The platform has publish/unpublish webhooks | V1 (freshness ≤ 15 min) | No webhooks: poll every 5 min plus a check at answer time that each cited article is still published |\n| Build vs buy | R2: weeks of build lost if we switch; buying puts transcripts and tuning on the vendor's side | Build a thin service on a hosted LLM API | No native bot from the help-center vendor meets V5 at lower total cost | Phase 0 desk comparison of vendor per-resolution pricing; in Phase 3, run the vendor bot (if one exists) on the V5 eval set | The vendor bot passes V5 and costs per resolution ≤ our V6 figure: buy it, and keep the eval set and guardrail tests as acceptance tests |\n| Data-privacy boundary | R3: personal data sent to a vendor, or trained on, cannot be recalled | Hosted API under a DPA (no training, zero or minimal retention, region-pinned if required). Presidio redacts card numbers, government IDs, and similar before the LLM call and before logging. Handoff contact details go in a form field and never reach the LLM. Transcripts live in our Postgres with a TTL | Vendor terms and region meet our privacy commitments | V3 | V3 fails, or residency can't be met: switch to a regional endpoint or vendor, or self-host (re-plan) |\n| Corpus boundary (what is indexed) | R3: showing internal articles to the public cannot be undone | Index only published, publicly visible articles, filtered at ingestion (not at query time) | Article visibility is exposed by the API | V1 | Segment-restricted articles are needed: add per-user access filtering at retrieval, with identity (new R3 gate) |\n| Answer scope and abstention | R3: the company may be held to what the bot says | Answer only from retrieved passages, with validated citations. Abstain and offer handoff when the docs don't cover the question. Sensitive topics (refund or credit commitments, legal, security incidents, account-specific questions) get a fixed template plus handoff | Grounded generation can meet the V5 bar | V5 | V5 fails: fall back to search with extracted snippets (no free-text generation) |\n| Prompt+RAG vs fine-tune | R2 for fine-tuning; R3 if trained on transcripts | Prompt+RAG | Docs change often, citations need retrieval, and fine-tuning can't track edits (cited basis) | V4/V5 | V4 passes but V5 fails on tone or format: fine-tune on curated, non-personal examples only |\n| Hosted API vs self-host | R2: the provider seam exists from Phase 0 | Hosted API behind a `ModelClient` interface, with a fallback model | Hosted terms and cost are acceptable | V3, V6 | V3 fails on residency, or V6 fails at volume |\n\n**R1 defaults:** monolith vs services → one deployable with a separate ingestion worker process; sync vs async → answers streamed synchronously over SSE, ingestion async from a queue table; vector store → pgvector in managed Postgres (corpus assumed under 10k articles); embedding model → pinned inside the index version (re-embedding takes hours at this size); search → hybrid (Postgres full-text + vector), with a reranker only if V4 needs it; feature flags → Unleash or LaunchDarkly; eval harness → promptfoo or pytest in CI.\n**N/A:** migration strategy and cutover — nothing is being replaced. The contact form and search stay as the permanent fallback.\n\n**Inherited constraints:** the help center is the system of record for content, and the bot never edits it (changing that would mean a new content workflow). The ticketing system is the system of record for escalations.\n\n## 4. Walking skeleton (Phase 0)\n- **Request:** an allow-listed support agent, signed in with company SSO, asks a real question (\"How do I reset my two-factor authentication?\") in the widget on the production help center. The widget appears only when the feature flag is on. The agent gets a streamed answer citing the source article, plus a \"Talk to a human\" link to the existing contact form.\n- **Tiers:** widget → chat API (SSO-checked) → retrieval over a pgvector index built by one real ingestion run of public articles through the help-center API → hosted LLM through `ModelClient` → answer rendered with citations → transcript and trace written to Postgres.\n- **Already in place on day zero:**\n  - The system prompt is kept apart from user text and retrieved text. Retrieved passages go in a delimited data block and are treated as data, never as instructions.\n  - The renderer allows links only to the help-center domain and renders no images or raw HTML.\n  - Hard token caps apply per turn and per session, and the provider-side spend limit is set on the key.\n- **Deploy / log / monitor / rollback:** container built in CI and deployed by IaC (Terraform) to production. OpenTelemetry carries one trace ID from widget to LLM. Metrics cover tokens, cost, latency, and error rate, with alerts on error rate and spend. Rollback means redeploying the previous image digest, with the flag off as the kill switch.\n- **Live-path baseline:** record the current help-center → contact-form rate, ticket volume per topic, and CSAT as BASELINE values for V6. Confirm the help-center and ticketing APIs (turn the ASSUMED rows to CONFIRMED). Start the organizational items: DPA, ticket-data access, named owners, cost-per-ticket input.\n- **Who can reach it:** allow-listed staff only. No customer traffic and no customer data.\n- **Exit check (V0):** see §6.\n\n## 5. Phases\n\n**Phase 1 — Defenses and budgets**\n- Unlocks: any exposure path. Phases 2–3 can be built against a guarded system.\n- Depends on: V0.\n- Tasks:\n  1. Corpus-boundary filter at ingestion, plus a diff of indexed IDs against the public listing on every sync.\n  2. Unpublish handled as a priority delete.\n  3. Injection suite in CI covering user turns and a planted test article in a staging index.\n  4. Presidio redaction before the LLM call and before logs.\n  5. Sensitive-topic classifier routing to the handoff template.\n  6. Caps on tokens per turn and turns per session. A daily spend kill switch that turns the flag off automatically. Timeout leading to the degraded \"matching articles\" response. Circuit breaker on the LLM.\n  7. Human-in-the-loop rule: the model has no tools. Ticket creation runs only from the user's confirmed button click in the UI handler, never from model output.\n  8. Transcripts classified as customer personal data, with restricted access and a TTL.\n- Rollback: guardrail config is versioned; revert it with a redeploy.\n- Exit check: V1 and V2 pass. A synthetic runaway session is cut off at the cap and emits a cost metric.\n\n**Phase 2 — Retrieval**\n- Unlocks: answer tuning.\n- Depends on: Phase 1 and the eval-data access approval.\n- Tasks:\n  1. Chunk schema: article section with heading path, plus metadata (article ID, locale, product, updated_at, visibility).\n  2. Index version = embedding model + chunker version + corpus snapshot.\n  3. Hybrid search.\n  4. Labeled eval set of at least 200 PII-scrubbed real questions with their source passages, plus at least 100 questions the docs don't answer.\n  5. Content-gap report to the docs owner.\n- Rollback: blue/green index swap, keeping the previous index version.\n- Exit check: V4 passes.\n\n**Phase 3 — Model access, memory, orchestration (answer generation)**\n- Unlocks: a customer canary.\n- Depends on: V4.\n- Tasks:\n  1. One fixed chain: rewrite the follow-up into a standalone query, retrieve, generate structured output (answer, citations[], abstain flag), then validate the citations. Each citation must be a passage that was actually retrieved and is still published. Failing validation means abstain.\n  2. Conversation memory within the session only (last N turns).\n  3. Fallback model selectable by config.\n  4. Retries with backoff.\n  5. Versioned prompt registry.\n  6. Build-vs-buy bake-off on the same eval set.\n- Rollback: pin the previous prompt + model + index version.\n- Exit check: V5 passes on the primary and the fallback model. Operations stay within the complexity budget.\n\n**Phase 4 — Handoff and customer canary**\n- Unlocks: measuring real resolution and cost.\n- Depends on: V1, V2, V3, V5, and the throughput input.\n- Tasks:\n  1. Ticketing handoff: the user confirms a ticket that carries the redacted transcript, with a scoped API token.\n  2. Brief the support agents.\n  3. Load test at 2× the projected canary peak.\n  4. Per-IP and per-session rate limits, with a CAPTCHA when abuse is detected.\n  5. Canary to 1%, then 5%, of anonymous English help-center visitors, assigned deterministically by cohort. The contact form stays visible.\n  6. Auto-disable the flag on a breach of the error, spend, or complaint threshold.\n- Rollback: flag off, which drops customers back to the existing path at no cost.\n- Exit check: V6 passes.\n\n**Phase 5 — Widen and feedback**\n- Unlocks: general availability.\n- Depends on: V6 and the SLO input.\n- Tasks:\n  1. Widen to 25%, 50%, then 100%. Each step is held until its dashboard check passes against the Phase 0 BASELINE.\n  2. Capture thumbs up/down and agent-tagged \"bot was wrong\" on handed-off tickets.\n  3. Weekly human review feeds corrections into the eval set and doc fixes. Nothing is applied to prompts automatically.\n  4. SLIs and burn-rate alerts.\n  5. Quarterly red-team.\n- Rollback: step back down the canary ladder, or turn the flag off.\n- Exit check: the SLO is met for 30 days. Each feedback-driven change improves the eval with no regressions.\n\n## 6. Validation gates\n\n| ID | Hypothesis | Method | Acceptance threshold | Evidence | Unlocks (and if it fails) | Phase |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| V0 | A change can be deployed, observed, and rolled back through every tier in production | Real staff question end to end; deploy and roll back through the pipeline; block the LLM endpoint to inject a failure | One trace spans widget → LLM. Latency, tokens, and cost recorded as BASELINE floors | Trace link, pipeline run log, alert record, baseline sheet in the repo | Phase 1 | 0 |\n| V1 | Only published public articles are indexed, and retractions propagate fast | Diff indexed IDs against the anonymous public API on every sync; planted restricted test article; timed unpublish test | 0 non-public articles indexed (ASSUMPTION: zero tolerance is the only safe bar for internal content); unpublish reflected ≤ 15 min (ASSUMPTION) | Sync diff logs; test report in CI | Phase 4 exposure. Fails: no canary; fix the filter or switch to polling | 1 |\n| V2 | Injection via user text or doc text cannot leak data or trigger actions | ≥ 100 cases (public injection corpora + red-team cases) in CI, plus one security-lead red-team session | By design, 0 cases emit an off-domain URL or image, reveal the system prompt or another session's data, or create a ticket. Stays on-task in ≥ 95% of jailbreak cases (ASSUMPTION). Security lead's pass/fail sign-off | CI suite report per build; signed red-team notes | Phase 4. Fails: block exposure, tighten the renderer and prompt separation | 1 |\n| V3 | Sending customer chat text to the vendor and storing transcripts is permitted | Privacy/legal review of the data-flow diagram; DPA executed; PII scanner run on logs and traces using planted synthetic PII | Privacy owner's pass/fail sign-off; 0 planted card numbers or IDs found in logs, traces, or vendor payloads | Signed DPA, data-flow record, scan report | Phase 4. Fails: change region or vendor, or self-host (re-plan) | starts 0, required before 4 |\n| V4 | For answerable questions, retrieval returns the supporting passage | Eval set of ≥ 200 real questions (Phase 2), run per index version in CI | Hit rate@5 ≥ 0.85 (ASSUMPTION: curated corpus with hybrid search; about ±5 points of sampling error at n=200) | Eval report per index version in CI artifacts | Phase 3 tuning. Fails: re-chunk, add a reranker, or log the misses as content gaps | 2 |\n| V5 | Answers are grounded, abstain when uncovered, and hand off sensitive topics (**guards the worst failure**) | V4 set + ≥ 100 unanswerable + ≥ 50 sensitive-topic questions. Automated citation validity; LLM-judge faithfulness calibrated against support-lead labels on 100 answers; blind review | Unsupported-claim rate ≤ 2% (ASSUMPTION); abstention on unanswerable ≥ 90% (ASSUMPTION); sensitive topics routed to handoff in 100% of the test set (ASSUMPTION). Fails: flip to search with snippets | 3 |\n| V6 | The bot resolves conversations for less than human handling, without hurting CSAT | 5% canary for 2 weeks. \"Resolved\" = no ticket or re-contact on the topic within 72 h and no thumbs-down | Cost per resolved conversation < human cost per ticket (UNKNOWN: support lead supplies it before Phase 4); CSAT and re-contact no worse than the Phase 0 BASELINE | Canary dashboard export (counts only, no transcripts) | Phase 5 widening. Fails: narrow the scope, add a cheaper-model route, or stay at canary | 4, required before 5 |\n\n## 7. Cross-cutting concerns\n\n| Phase | Security | Observability | Reproducibility | Resilience |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 0 | SSO allow-list; secrets in a vault; vendor spend limit; prompt/data separation; link allow-list renderer | OTel trace end to end; token, cost, and latency metrics; error and spend alerts | IaC; image digest, model version, prompt version, and index version stamped on every trace | Timeout → degraded response; flag kill switch; rollback rehearsed |\n| 1 | Corpus filter; Presidio redaction; injection suite; no model-callable tools | Guardrail-trigger and abstention metrics; per-session cost; logs classified as personal data with restricted access | Guardrail config and injection suite versioned in CI | Spend kill switch; session caps; LLM circuit breaker |\n| 2 | Eval data scrubbed and kept in a restricted store; read-only ingestion credentials | Sync lag, index freshness, retrieval scores per request | Index rebuildable from the help center plus a pinned version | Blue/green index swap; nightly reconcile |\n| 3 | Citation validator; structured output; sensitive-topic template | Citation validity, abstention rate, sampled online judge scores | Prompt registry; eval run per version | Fallback model; retries; abstain when validation fails |\n| 4 | Rate limits and CAPTCHA; scoped ticketing token; DPA in force | Canary dashboard: resolution, handoff, re-contact, CSAT, cost per resolved conversation | Deterministic cohort assignment; flag config versioned | Load test; auto-disable on breach; contact-form fallback |\n| 5 | Feedback reviewed before it changes anything (poisoning path closed); quarterly red-team | SLO burn-rate alerts; content-gap report | Feedback → eval set changes versioned | Capacity checked at each widening step; provider failover drill |\n\n## 8. AI layer\n\n| Sublayer | In this system | Built in | Exit check or V-ID |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1. Injection / guardrail defense | Prompt/data separation, link-only renderer, PII redaction, corpus boundary, sensitive-topic routing | 0 (baseline), 1 | V1, V2 |\n| 2. Cost + latency budget | Token, turn, and daily spend caps; timeout with degraded response | 0 (caps), 1 | Phase 1 exit check; V6 |\n| 3. Human-in-the-loop | The model has no tools; tickets are created only on the user's confirmed click; humans take over at handoff | 1, 4 | V2 (no ticket created by the model) |\n| 4. Memory | Last N turns within the session only; no memory across sessions | 3 | V5 includes follow-up questions |\n| 7. Routing | Not needed: one model plus a fallback (sensitive-topic handoff is a guardrail, not routing) | — | — |\n| 9. Deliberately deferred\n- **Account-aware answers and actions (order status, refunds):** pulled forward if the business needs them. Requires identity, an authorization design, a tool allow-list, and approval gates for writes.\n- **Segment-restricted or logged-in-only articles:** pulled forward if more than about 10% of handed-off questions are covered only by restricted articles. Requires per-user access filtering (new R3 gate).\n- **Languages other than English:** pulled forward if the canary shows meaningful non-English demand. Needs locale eval sets per language.\n- **Memory across sessions:** pulled forward if users need to resume conversations. The contact-form fallback counts as degraded but available | Phase 5 SLO + burn-rate alerts |\n| AI inference cost: hard caps | ≤ 6k input + 600 output tokens per turn; ≤ 15 turns per session; daily spend cap on the API key set at 2× the measured Phase 0 daily spend | Design parameters (caps I chose, not business targets) | Phase 1 exit check |\n| AI inference cost: per resolved conversation | — | UNKNOWN: needs the fully loaded human cost per ticket (support lead), before Phase 4 | V6 |\n| Index freshness | An edited or unpublished article is reflected in answers within 15 min | ASSUMPTION: a retracted policy must stop being cited quickly; confirm with the docs owner | V1 |\n| Transcript retention | 30 days, then delete | ASSUMPTION: a conservative stopgap until the privacy owner sets the policy (before Phase 4) | V3 |\n| Operational complexity | One service (API + ingestion worker), one managed Postgres with pgvector, one hosted LLM API; no self-hosted model or vector cluster | ASSUMPTION: one small team owns it | Phase 3 exit check |\n\n**Missing inputs** (most plan-changing first):\n1. **Account-aware answers or actions in v1?** I assumed no (see top).\n2. **Help-center platform and its API.** Is it Zendesk Guide, Intercom, Salesforce Knowledge, Confluence, or a static site? Does it have publish/unpublish webhooks? Does it have internal-only or segment-restricted articles? I assumed restricted articles exist, so v1 indexes public articles only.\n3. **Customer regions and languages.** EU customers bring GDPR and possibly data-residency requirements, which constrain the LLM vendor (V3). I assumed v1 is English only.\n4. **Ticketing system for handoff** and its API access.\n5. **Volume, human cost per ticket, SLO.** Needed for the UNKNOWN rows above.\n6. **Real questions for the eval set.** These come from historical tickets and help-center search logs, which contain personal data, so a data-access approval is needed.\n7. **Named owners:** support lead (answer quality sign-off), docs owner (content gaps), security lead (red team), privacy/legal (vendor terms, disclaimer, topics the bot may answer).\n\n## 2. Dependency map\n\n| What waits | Depends on | Kind | Blocked from being |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Any customer text reaching the LLM vendor (Phase 4) | Signed data processing agreement (DPA) with no-training / zero-retention terms; privacy review of the data flow (V3) | organizational + risk-security, ASSUMED not yet in place | exposed (starts Phase 0) |\n| Eval sets for V4 and V5 | Approval to use historical tickets and search logs; PII scrubbing | organizational, ASSUMED | built (starts Phase 0, needed by Phase 2) |\n| Prompt and answer-format tuning (Phase 3) | V4 retrieval hit rate | validation | specified |\n| Customer canary (Phase 4) | V1 corpus boundary, V2 injection containment, V3 privacy, V5 grounding | risk-security | exposed |\n| Topic policy (what the bot must hand off) and disclaimer text | Legal + support lead sign-off (in V5) | organizational | exposed |\n| Index sync design | Help-center API and webhooks | structural/runtime, ASSUMED | specified |\n| Handoff to a human with transcript (Phase 4) | Scoped ticketing API token; support ops agreement on routing | organizational, ASSUMED | deployed |\n| Widening past the canary (Phase 5) | V6 cost per resolved conversation; human cost-per-ticket input | economic | scaled |\n| Load test (Phase 4) | Throughput input (analytics) | organizational | specified |\n\nAll seven kinds bind. Nothing existing depends on the bot. The bot depends on the help center and the ticketing system (both ASSUMED until Phase 0 confirms their APIs).\n\n## 3. Tradeoff gates (resolved up front)\n\n| Decision | Reversibility | Default (chosen now) | Assumption | Validated by | Flip condition |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Consistency vs availability (index vs help center) | R2: citing a retracted policy hurts customers, but the index can be rebuilt | Eventually consistent: webhook-driven incremental sync, a nightly full reconcile, and unpublish handled as a priority delete | The platform has publish/unpublish webhooks | V1 (freshness ≤ 15 min) | No webhooks: poll every 5 min plus a check at answer time that each cited article is still published |\n| Build vs buy | R2: weeks of build lost if we switch; buying puts transcripts and tuning on the vendor's side | Build a thin service on a hosted LLM API | No native bot from the help-center vendor meets V5 at lower total cost | Phase 0 desk comparison of vendor per-resolution pricing; in Phase 3, run the vendor bot (if one exists) on the V5 eval set | The vendor bot passes V5 and costs per resolution ≤ our V6 figure: buy it, and keep the eval set and guardrail tests as acceptance tests |\n| Data-privacy boundary | R3: personal data sent to a vendor, or trained on, cannot be recalled | Hosted API under a DPA (no training, zero or minimal retention, region-pinned if required). Presidio redacts card numbers, government IDs, and similar before the LLM call and before logging. Handoff contact details go in a form field and never reach the LLM. Transcripts live in our Postgres with a TTL | Vendor terms and region meet our privacy commitments | V3 | V3 fails, or residency can't be met: switch to a regional endpoint or vendor, or self-host (re-plan) |\n| Corpus boundary (what is indexed) | R3: showing internal articles to the public cannot be undone | Index only published, publicly visible articles, filtered at ingestion (not at query time) | Article visibility is exposed by the API | V1 | Segment-restricted articles are needed: add per-user access filtering at retrieval, with identity (new R3 gate) |\n| Answer scope and abstention | R3: the company may be held to what the bot says | Answer only from retrieved passages, with validated citations. Abstain and offer handoff when the docs don't cover the question. Sensitive topics (refund or credit commitments, legal, security incidents, account-specific questions) get a fixed template plus handoff | Grounded generation can meet the V5 bar | V5 | V5 fails: fall back to search with extracted snippets (no free-text generation) |\n| Prompt+RAG vs fine-tune | R2 for fine-tuning; R3 if trained on transcripts | Prompt+RAG | Docs change often, citations need retrieval, and fine-tuning can't track edits (cited basis) | V4/V5 | V4 passes but V5 fails on tone or format: fine-tune on curated, non-personal examples only |\n| Hosted API vs self-host | R2: the provider seam exists from Phase 0 | Hosted API behind a `ModelClient` interface, with a fallback model | Hosted terms and cost are acceptable | V3, V6 | V3 fails on residency, or V6 fails at volume |\n\n**R1 defaults:** monolith vs services → one deployable with a separate ingestion worker process; sync vs async → answers streamed synchronously over SSE, ingestion async from a queue table; vector store → pgvector in managed Postgres (corpus assumed under 10k articles); embedding model → pinned inside the index version (re-embedding takes hours at this size); search → hybrid (Postgres full-text + vector), with a reranker only if V4 needs it; feature flags → Unleash or LaunchDarkly; eval harness → promptfoo or pytest in CI.\n**N/A:** migration strategy and cutover — nothing is being replaced. The contact form and search stay as the permanent fallback.\n\n**Inherited constraints:** the help center is the system of record for content, and the bot never edits it (changing that would mean a new content workflow). The ticketing system is the system of record for escalations.\n\n## 4. Walking skeleton (Phase 0)\n- **Request:** an allow-listed support agent, signed in with company SSO, asks a real question (\"How do I reset my two-factor authentication?\") in the widget on the production help center. The widget appears only when the feature flag is on. The agent gets a streamed answer citing the source article, plus a \"Talk to a human\" link to the existing contact form.\n- **Tiers:** widget → chat API (SSO-checked) → retrieval over a pgvector index built by one real ingestion run of public articles through the help-center API → hosted LLM through `ModelClient` → answer rendered with citations → transcript and trace written to Postgres.\n- **Already in place on day zero:**\n  - The system prompt is kept apart from user text and retrieved text. Retrieved passages go in a delimited data block and are treated as data, never as instructions.\n  - The renderer allows links only to the help-center domain and renders no images or raw HTML.\n  - Hard token caps apply per turn and per session, and the provider-side spend limit is set on the key.\n- **Deploy / log / monitor / rollback:** container built in CI and deployed by IaC (Terraform) to production. OpenTelemetry carries one trace ID from widget to LLM. Metrics cover tokens, cost, latency, and error rate, with alerts on error rate and spend. Rollback means redeploying the previous image digest, with the flag off as the kill switch.\n- **Live-path baseline:** record the current help-center → contact-form rate, ticket volume per topic, and CSAT as BASELINE values for V6. Confirm the help-center and ticketing APIs (turn the ASSUMED rows to CONFIRMED). Start the organizational items: DPA, ticket-data access, named owners, cost-per-ticket input.\n- **Who can reach it:** allow-listed staff only. No customer traffic and no customer data.\n- **Exit check (V0):** see §6.\n\n## 5. Phases\n\n**Phase 1 — Defenses and budgets**\n- Unlocks: any exposure path. Phases 2–3 can be built against a guarded system.\n- Depends on: V0.\n- Tasks:\n  1. Corpus-boundary filter at ingestion, plus a diff of indexed IDs against the public listing on every sync.\n  2. Unpublish handled as a priority delete.\n  3. Injection suite in CI covering user turns and a planted test article in a staging index.\n  4. Presidio redaction before the LLM call and before logs.\n  5. Sensitive-topic classifier routing to the handoff template.\n  6. Caps on tokens per turn and turns per session. A daily spend kill switch that turns the flag off automatically. Timeout leading to the degraded \"matching articles\" response. Circuit breaker on the LLM.\n  7. Human-in-the-loop rule: the model has no tools. Ticket creation runs only from the user's confirmed button click in the UI handler, never from model output.\n  8. Transcripts classified as customer personal data, with restricted access and a TTL.\n- Rollback: guardrail config is versioned; revert it with a redeploy.\n- Exit check: V1 and V2 pass. A synthetic runaway session is cut off at the cap and emits a cost metric.\n\n**Phase 2 — Retrieval**\n- Unlocks: answer tuning.\n- Depends on: Phase 1 and the eval-data access approval.\n- Tasks:\n  1. Chunk schema: article section with heading path, plus metadata (article ID, locale, product, updated_at, visibility).\n  2. Index version = embedding model + chunker version + corpus snapshot.\n  3. Hybrid search.\n  4. Labeled eval set of at least 200 PII-scrubbed real questions with their source passages, plus at least 100 questions the docs don't answer.\n  5. Content-gap report to the docs owner.\n- Rollback: blue/green index swap, keeping the previous index version.\n- Exit check: V4 passes.\n\n**Phase 3 — Model access, memory, orchestration (answer generation)**\n- Unlocks: a customer canary.\n- Depends on: V4.\n- Tasks:\n  1. One fixed chain: rewrite the follow-up into a standalone query, retrieve, generate structured output (answer, citations[], abstain flag), then validate the citations. Each citation must be a passage that was actually retrieved and is still published. Failing validation means abstain.\n  2. Conversation memory within the session only (last N turns).\n  3. Fallback model selectable by config.\n  4. Retries with backoff.\n  5. Versioned prompt registry.\n  6. Build-vs-buy bake-off on the same eval set.\n- Rollback: pin the previous prompt + model + index version.\n- Exit check: V5 passes on the primary and the fallback model. Operations stay within the complexity budget.\n\n**Phase 4 — Handoff and customer canary**\n- Unlocks: measuring real resolution and cost.\n- Depends on: V1, V2, V3, V5, and the throughput input.\n- Tasks:\n  1. Ticketing handoff: the user confirms a ticket that carries the redacted transcript, with a scoped API token.\n  2. Brief the support agents.\n  3. Load test at 2× the projected canary peak.\n  4. Per-IP and per-session rate limits, with a CAPTCHA when abuse is detected.\n  5. Canary to 1%, then 5%, of anonymous English help-center visitors, assigned deterministically by cohort. The contact form stays visible.\n  6. Auto-disable the flag on a breach of the error, spend, or complaint threshold.\n- Rollback: flag off, which drops customers back to the existing path at no cost.\n- Exit check: V6 passes.\n\n**Phase 5 — Widen and feedback**\n- Unlocks: general availability.\n- Depends on: V6 and the SLO input.\n- Tasks:\n  1. Widen to 25%, 50%, then 100%. Each step is held until its dashboard check passes against the Phase 0 BASELINE.\n  2. Capture thumbs up/down and agent-tagged \"bot was wrong\" on handed-off tickets.\n  3. Weekly human review feeds corrections into the eval set and doc fixes. Nothing is applied to prompts automatically.\n  4. SLIs and burn-rate alerts.\n  5. Quarterly red-team.\n- Rollback: step back down the canary ladder, or turn the flag off.\n- Exit check: the SLO is met for 30 days. Each feedback-driven change improves the eval with no regressions.\n\n## 6. Deliberately deferred\n- **Account-aware answers and actions (order status, refunds):** pulled forward if the business needs them. Requires identity, an authorization design, a tool allow-list, and approval gates for writes.\n- **Segment-restricted or logged-in-only articles:** pulled forward if more than about 10% of handed-off questions are covered only by restricted articles. Requires per-user access filtering (new R3 gate).\n- **Languages other than English:** pulled forward if the canary shows meaningful non-English demand. Needs locale eval sets per language.\n- **Memory across sessions:** pulled forward if users need to resume conversations.
